# Welcome {-}

This is the landing page for the **"Single-cell RNA-seq analysis with
R/Bioconductor"** workshop organised by [Physalia](https://www.physalia-courses.org/),
**2026 edition**.

It gathers all the lectures and hands-on labs of the course. Every lab can be
run in the cloud, in your web browser, with nothing to install: see
[Getting started](pages/getting-started.qmd).

## What {-}

This course will introduce biologists and bioinformaticians to the field of
single-cell RNA sequencing. We will cover a range of software and analysis
workflows that extend over the spectrum from the best practices in the
filtering scRNA-seq data to the downstream analysis of cell clusters and
temporal ordering. This course will help the attendees gain accurate insights
in pre-processing, analysis and interpretation of scRNA-seq data.

We will start by introducing general concepts about single-cell RNA-sequencing.
From there, we will then continue to describe the main analysis steps to go
from raw sequencing data to processed and usable data. We will present
classical analysis workflows, their output and the possible paths to
investigate downstream of this.

Throughout the workshop, `bash` tools and `R/Bioconductor` packages will be
used to analyse datasets and learn new approaches.

## When {-}

<!-- TODO: update with the dates of the 2026 edition -->
**Dates of the 2026 edition: to be announced.** Classes run from 14:00 to
20:00 (Paris time), over five days.

## Where {-}

This course will be held online. All the hands-on labs run in the cloud, on
the [Bioconductor Orchestra platform](https://orchestraplatform.org/):
each participant gets their own `RStudio` session, in their web browser,
started from the Docker image built from this book.

## How {-}

The course is structured in modules over five days. Each day will include
formal lectures covering the key concepts required to understand scRNA-seq
analysis. The remainder of each day will consist in practical hands-on sessions
focusing on analysis of scRNA-seq data. These sessions will involve a
combination of both mirroring exercises with the instructor to demonstrate a
skill, as well as applying these skills on your own to complete individual
exercises. During and after each exercise, interpretation of results will be
discussed as a group.

## Who {-}

The course will be mostly beneficial to those who have, or will shortly have,
scRNA-seq data ready to analyse.

The material is suitable both for experimentalists who want to learn more about
data-analysis as well as computational biologists who want to learn about
scRNA-seq methods.

Examples demonstrated in this course can be applied to any experimental
protocol or biological system.

The requirements for this course are:

1.  Working knowledge of Unix / command line interface (managing files, running programs, reading manuals!). Basic bash commands (`cd`, `ls`, `...`) and CLI usage will *not* be covered in this course. We advice attendees to not register if they lack fundamental experience in CLI.
2.  Programming experience in `R` (writing a function, basic I/O operations, variable types, using packages). `Bioconductor` experience is a plus.
3.  Familiarity with next-generation sequencing data and its analyses (using alignment and quantification tools for bulk sequencing data)

See the [Prerequisites](pages/prerequisites.qmd) page for refresher material.

## Why {-}

At the end of this course, you should be able to:

-   Understand the pros/cons of different single-cell RNA-seq methods
-   Process and QC of scRNA-seq data
-   Normalize scRNA-seq data
-   Correct for batch effects
-   Visualise the data and applying dimensionality reduction
-   Perform cell clustering and annotation
-   Perform differential gene expression analysis
-   Infer cell trajectory and pseudotime, and perform temporal differential expression

Throughout the course, we will also have a focus on reproducible research,
documented content and interactive reports.

# Docker image {-}

This book is a [`BiocBook`](https://github.com/js2264/BiocBook): every
version of the book comes with a `Docker` image providing `R`, `Bioconductor`,
every package and command-line tool used in the labs, and the datasets they
use. This is the image the workshop sessions run on Orchestra. It is available
here:

👉 [ghcr.io/js2264/scrnaseqphysalia2026](https://github.com/js2264/scRNAseq_Physalia_2026/pkgs/container/scrnaseqphysalia2026) 🐳

::: {.callout-tip icon='true'}
## Get started now 🎉

You can get access to all the packages used in this book in < 1 minute,
using this command in a terminal:

```{sh "docker", filename="bash"}
#| eval: false
docker run -it ghcr.io/js2264/scrnaseqphysalia2026:devel R
```

:::

# RStudio Server {-}

An RStudio Server instance can be initiated from the `Docker` image as follows:

```{sh "rstudio", filename="bash"}
#| eval: false
docker run \
    --volume <local_folder>:<destination_folder> \
    -e PASSWORD=physalia \
    -p 8787:8787 \
    ghcr.io/js2264/scrnaseqphysalia2026:devel
```

The initiated RStudio Server instance will be available at
[http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787) (user: `rstudio`, password:
`physalia`). See [Getting started](pages/getting-started.qmd) for more details.
